_comment: Navigation sweep profile for The Flintstones: The Surprise at Dinosaur
Peak! (ADR-0239, PRD Part A slice F14.18). Read by
scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 s1 says to take the first rung that reaches
the place, and this game's first rung is its own hidden debug level select:
a fourteen-press button code typed at the title screen, no cheat at all.
navigation.kind is 'input', so no session carries a pin and every session
is an ADR-0184 s2 'clean' pass. Rung 2 is not available on this game and
not merely unwanted: NO RAM MAP IS PUBLISHED FOR IT. Data Crystal's game
page has no /RAM_map subpage (checked 2026-09-26 through the Wayback
Machine, because tcrf.net and its datacrystal subdomain both answer a
Cloudflare challenge to curl), the ROM Detectives wiki has no page for it,
and the vendored UI/Dependencies/Internal/CheatDb.Nes.json names a
DIFFERENT DUMP - see the hash note below - so its 26 codes are not
evidence about this one. A RAM selector would therefore need an invented
address, which ADR-0184 s5 refuses.
THE SOURCE, VERBATIM. TCRF, 'The Flintstones: The Surprise at Dinosaur
Peak!', section 'Debug Mode' (https://tcrf.net/The_Flintstones:
The_Surprise_at_Dinosaur_Peak!, read 2026-09-26 through the Wayback
Machine snapshot 20260913031036; the live page is behind a JS challenge):
'Press A, B, Right, A, Down, Down, Down, Down, B, Left, Left, B, A,
Start at the title screen. Select NORMAL to start the game as normal,
or NOHIT to enable invincibility. After pressing any button, a number
will appear which acts as a combination sound test/stage select: press
Left or Right to change the number, A to play the selected sound, B to
stop, and Start to begin the game on the selected stage.'
'The code also enables two other debugging features: during gameplay,
press Up on Controller 2 to end the current level and mark it as
"passed" on the map screen, or Down to bring up the Game Over screen.'
'(Source: GameFAQs (Meweight), Rachel Mae)'
StrategyWiki, 'The Flintstones: The Surprise at Dinosaur Peak', names the
game's ten areas - Bedrock, Jungle, Mine, Sea, Slate and Gravel, Giant's
House, Witch's Tower, Pterodactyl Ride, Dinosaur Peak Exterior and
Dinosaur Peak Interior - and says levels must be played in a set order.
It does NOT map the debug number to any of them, and neither does TCRF,
nor the GameFAQs Game Genie list (Almar's Guides, 'Continue on Level
2...10'), which stops at level 10. The map below is therefore measured,
not quoted, and the titles name an area only where the screen itself
spells it out.
WHAT THE NUMBER IS, MEASURED. runs/f1418/flintstones/probe-steps.py runs
N presses of Right from the number screen (runs/f1418/flintstones/dbg0.mss,
minted by levels.py) with and without the Start that begins the game, and
reads three bytes off each run's own final state:
$03CE  on the number screen, EQUALS THE PRESS COUNT, binary (10 presses
-> 0A, 36 -> 24, 59 -> 3B). One press is one step, and the
screen draws the same number in decimal ('05' at 5, '50' at
50). It reads 00 before any press.
$05FB  00 on the number screen and equal to the press count after
Start, so it is the loader's copy of the number (n012 in
probe-steps: $03CE=0C, $05FB=00; the same N with Start:
$0303  THE LEVEL'S OWN BYTE, written by the level loader and read off
the level's data: 00 on the number screen, and equal to the
press count for 0..36 EXCEPT 12, which reads 0B (see below).
The counter wraps at 100, not at 60: 100 presses -> $03CE=00, 160 -> 3C
(= 60). So the screen accepts 100 values, 00..99.
HOW MANY OF THEM ARE PLACES: 37, the values 00..36. Measured two ways on
this checkout's dump, 2026-09-26:
* $0303 stops following the number at 37. 36 -> 24, 37 -> 22 (= 34),
13, 61 -> 13, 63 -> 00, 160 -> 13. A number that reads a level id it
did not dial is not dialling a level any more: the entry the loader
takes there is past the end of the game's own level table.
* the frames. runs/f1418/flintstones/levels/nNNN/ holds a screenshot
per value, all 43 of them distinct by playfield hash, and the two
closest pairs in the whole set are 32 ~ 39 (21 differing cells) and
34 ~ 37 (24) - both of them values past 36 landing back on a room an
in-range value already draws (34 and 32 respectively). Every pair
inside 0..36 differs by at least 54 of 736 8x8 cells, counted over the
playfield (the frame below y=56, box-filtered to 32x23 cell means)
with a cell differing when any channel differs by more than 24. So
37..99 re-enter or garble, and the set of places is 37.
THE COLLISION AT 12, AND WHY 12 IS STILL A VALUE. Selector 12 starts its
own level: 12 presses read $03CE=0C and $05FB=0C, its playfield is a
green-walled room with a blue pipe and spikes that value 11's blue
cavern does not draw, and 385 bytes of the two sessions' RAM differ. But
the level data 12 loads carries the id byte 0B - the same id 11's level
carries - so $0303 cannot tell the two sessions apart, and $030D is 07 in
12's (08 in every other value's). This is the game's own data saying two
levels share an id, the same shape as a level split across two entries;
it is written down rather than papered over, and the ramCheck below
carries the value the game really writes (0B), with the 0C that
separates it reported per session as $05FB in RESULT.md.
THE RAM CHECKS. Every value checks $0303 against the level's own id, the
byte this measurement gives it - '00'..'24', and '0B' for 12. It is a
check and not a cheat, so ADR-0184 s5's 'no code is invented' does not
bite, but the byte is not in any published RAM map (there is none): it
was found by diffing the sessions' final states, exactly as Super Mario
Bros. 3's $0348 was, and like that one it is only as good as this
measurement. What it proves is that the session left the number screen
and the loader ran: on the number screen with no Start, all 18 probe runs
that saved a final state (runs/f1418/flintstones/steps/n*/final.mss) read
$0303=00 while $03CE already read the dialled number. What it
does NOT prove is that the room is 12 rather than 11 - nothing in RAM
does, and the screenshot in runs/f1418/flintstones/levels/n012 is the
evidence for that one claim.
WHAT THE 120 s FINAL STATE READS, AND WHERE FIVE SESSIONS DEPART. $0303 is
the room the game is IN when the byte is read, not a latch of the room it
was sent to, and five of the 37 rooms end by themselves inside the run:
sessions 22, 27, 32, 33 and 34 finish reading 14, 1A, 01, 02 and 0B - rooms
the selector loads for other values - so their ramCheck reports the
departure instead of confirming the entry. The departure is the game's, not
the body's. runs/f1418/flintstones/drift.py measures it three ways: one
second after the level loads every one of the five still reads its own id,
with $03CE and $05FB agreeing; ONE pass of the blind body (518 f, 8.6 s)
leaves 22 and 27 on their own id but has already moved 32, 33 and 34; and
11 s of no input at all leaves all five on their own id. Walking is not the
cause either: re-run with a body that stands still
(runs/f1418/flintstones/trial-still-body, written by still-body.py) all five
still depart, and value 32 read its own 20 at 30 s after the load and 01 at
60 s with no input ever sent. Those rooms are scripted to end - a ride, a
scene, or a death and respawn - and the run is 120 s long, which is why
they are gone by the end. The check is left reading the id the game's own
level data gives the room the selector chose, '00'..'24' with '0B' for 12,
and the five departures are REPORTED rather than tuned away: an expected
byte taken from the session's own output would prove nothing (ADR-0239 s4).
Those five rows rest on the gate - new is 1251, 2019, 1115, 491 and 1010 -
plus the load-time witness in drift.py, not on the 120 s final state. The
still-body alternative was measured and rejected, not overlooked: it buys
no confirmation and costs drawn keys in all five rooms (3025, 3761, 2859,
2256 and 2779 keys walking against 2643, 2438, 2370, 2191 and 2491
standing).
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply: the pin
would need a published lives address and this game has no RAM map at all.
defaults.cheats is absent, no value declares one, and no process in this
sweep is launched with a cheat.
THE SECOND CONTROLLER LEVER IS MEASURED AND NOT REACHED. TCRF's 'Up on
Controller 2 ends the current level' was tried twice on 2026-09-26, from
level 00, with the sixteen-frame gap the game's own code needs
(runs/f1418/flintstones/p2-p2up.txt and p2-p2down.txt, 1976 frames each,
run through runs/f1418/flintstones/probe.py with the `-|U` and `-|D`
port-2 tokens that make the harness plug a pad into port 2, F9.22):
neither ended the level - both screenshots are the same opening room with
Fred standing in it (runs/f1418/flintstones/p2up-sheet.png and
p2down-sheet.png). So the map screen this profile would have used as a
second witness for the number-to-level map is not reached here either,
and the titles rest on the drawn screen alone.
CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SESSION. The selector picks a level, so a
session is ENTERED, never played to its end: the stage-clear transition,
the map screen and the ending are the part of the game this sweep leaves
to the game's own route. And the pack side is a CHR ROM game (128 KB PRG,
256 KB CHR, iNES mapper 4), so the builder writes a `defaultTile`
placeholder for every CHR index and the every-rule tile-data column is
saturated at the ROM's whole tile count in every pack of it; the written
rows and the `new` key count are the ones that move (ADR-0239 s4/s5,
THE ROM HASH IS THE LIBRARY DUMP'S, AND IT IS NOT THE CHEAT DB'S. The
No-Intro SHA1 above is D828853B47896F49A2563C48B131160B0E87941E, computed
on this checkout from the library file; the vendored cheat database names
'Flintstones, The - The Surprise at Dinosaur Peak! (USA)' at
E5D64AEDDD25952804AF5447C6898E9191DB1614. The database's sha1 field IS
the No-Intro hash - it agrees byte for byte with this repo's own sets for
Contra, Metroid, Castlevania and Life Force - so the two entries describe
two different dumps, and none of that entry's 26 codes is used here.

_defaultsComment: ADR-0239 s6's budget: 120 emulated seconds per session, the body repeated
to fill the run (build_sweep_script). The body is this set's only
recordable route as well, so the sweep presses the buttons the library
job's own route presses - one shape, two consumers.
The entry scripts are one mint per value because the number of Right
presses is the whole of the difference between them; room-entry.py
generates all 37 from that one template and `--check` fails if any file
is not what it would write. Each is 6 frames per press and 6 frames of
gap with a 60-frame pause either side of the Start that reveals the
number, measured on this dump: a press the screen is still reading is
dropped and the debug screen never appears, and a shorter pause before
that Start left the title screen up.
